p: to include the night of the last Yom Tov
"But say the night of the first Yom Tov?
I include the last Yom Tov,
And in this parashah there is not mentioned
only "You shall make the festival of Sukkos for yourself
and "You shall rejoice in your festival" (ibid. 13–14).
there is the change in the expression of joy
of joy of the festival of Sukkos:
it says, "You shall rejoice in your festival";
and regarding the four species it likewise says
וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם (וַיִּקְרָא כג, מ);
"And you shall rejoice before Hashem your God" (Vayikra 23:40);
and regarding the festival of Shavuos it likewise says
which is the matter of joy
from the person's side, to rejoice.
that you will be in joy.
And the matter is as they expounded
from the pasuk "And you shall sanctify yourselves
"And you shall sanctify yourselves" is from the person's side,
like "And you shall be only joyful."
that it is not within a person's power
to bring forth joy in his heart
except through the performance of a mitzvah,
such as through the four species
and through the mitzvah of sukkah;
about this it says, "You shall rejoice in your festival."
through the giving of the Torah.
there is no mitzvah at all in actual deed,
nor is it in remembrance of the past,
Rather, this is the root of the Yom Tov:
that Hashem Yisbarach causes joy to shine
in the inwardness of the point of the heart
That is, by there being absorbed
all the actions of the mitzvos
of the seven days of the festival,
into the inwardness of the point of the heart,
so that it may endure permanently.
And therefore they alluded in this
that through the joy that precedes it,
from the actions of the mitzvos,
the joy in the heart is increased of itself
on the last Yom Tov, from Above.
And therefore the name of the day is "Atzeres,"
into the inwardness of the heart
to endure for all the days of the year.
And to this there is an allusion
Yaakov is the head of the joy";
that is, the aspect of truth,
that is, the joy is made true
"The lip of truth shall be established forever."
And it says in the Midrash
that Shemini Atzeres ought to have been
That is, at the Exodus from Egypt
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
who took them out from the depths of the opposite,
and "a maidservant saw at the Sea," etc.
only that it was immediately hidden from them,
which is the aspect of "Binah is the heart,"
for the holiness to be absorbed
into the inwardness of the heart.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן לְאַחַר ז׳ יְמֵי הֶחָג
And likewise, after the seven days of the festival,
that they should be considered, of themselves,
and immediately on the eighth day we come
which is the aspect of Binah
in the inwardness of the point of the heart.
Now, it says in the Ohr HaChaim
that the main sustaining of the world
in all of the six weekdays
is from the holiness of the Shabbos that has passed;
וְאִם לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם
and if there were no person in the world
כִּי הֲלֹא הַדּוֹרוֹת שֶׁל בְּנֵי נֹחַ
for the generations of the descendants of Noach
up until Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
so on what did the world stand?
that the day of Shabbos itself
for the six weekdays that follow,
by way of the aspect of the Upper Shabbos,
which is the aspect of Binah,
as at the beginning of Creation,
that preceded the six days of work
which is the aspect of Binah, the upper Hei,
And it is the aspect of teshuvah:
before the seven days of Creation,
which are the seven holy middos.
And the Torah preceded by two thousand years;
for the Torah issues from Chochmah.
the source of the six days of building.
And the Shabbos that comes after
is the aspect of the lower Hei:
the revelation of His kingship, Yisbarach, in actuality;
and it is the aspect of yiras Shamayim.
And so too is the conduct of the world:
there shines forth the aspect of
the revelation of His kingship, Yisbarach,
which is the aspect of the lower Hei,
when he considers that the King,
immediately there will come upon him
And on the day of Shabbos
in the inwardness of the point of the heart
from the aspect of the upper Hei,
for the six weekdays that follow.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בִּגְמַר שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הֶחָג,
And likewise, at the close of the seven days of the festival,
there is revealed the aspect of His kingship, Yisbarach,
the aspect of fear, from the lower Hei,
David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
in whom shone forth fear and submission
from the revelation of the kingship of Heaven;
And after this we come to the eighth day,
which is the aspect of Binah,
and here it is from Above to below,
so that the joy is absorbed
into the inwardness of the heart, as mentioned above.
And it says in the Midrash
עַל קָרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁל ז׳ יְמֵי הֶחָג:
regarding the offerings of the seven days of the festival:
a parable of a king who said to his servants,
he said to his beloved friend,
in the application of the parable
is aimed at the nations of the world,
for whom seventy bulls are offered.
But surely the nations of the world
so how does the expression fit,
"he said to his servants, Make," etc.?
and "his beloved friend" refer to Yisrael;
only that during the seven days of the festival
we are designated by the name "servants,"
since all the drawing down of holiness and joy
"And if I am a master," etc.;
for they are occupied with the building of the world.
And consequently it is also needed
for such was the order of Creation
in the seven days of building.
And when we reach the day of Shemini Atzeres,
like the love of a son for his father,
even without any intermediary of service;
like the holiness of this day,
which is without the coloring of any mitzvah,
only their bond to Him, Yisbarach,
And as the holy Zohar concludes (ibid.):
'Fortunate are you, Yisrael, who is like you,
